title: Sampling-Based Planning: Probabilistic Roadmaps and RRT

contract.reader: An engineer or student who has read entries 1 and 2 and needs to plan for robots with more than two or three degrees of freedom
contract.problem: Grids do not scale with dimension; which sampling planner to use, what its guarantees mean and when it fails
contract.outcome: Build a PRM and an RRT on a collision checker; read probabilistic completeness and asymptotic optimality correctly; set the PRM* radius or k; recognize narrow passages and choose a sampling strategy; shorten a path
contract.contribution: The same planner code run on a point in a room and on the two-link arm on the torus, reported over 10 or 20 seeds against a known optimum
contract.evidence: Programs with real output and seeds, Kavraki et al. 1996, LaValle 1998, Kuffner and LaValle 2000, Karaman and Frazzoli 2011, Solovey et al. 2020 and others (numbers recomputed in the 2026-10-24 live review)
contract.limitations: Two-dimensional examples; differential constraints out of scope; RRT* radius a stated demonstration choice

findings.location: Sections 2.3, 3.2, 3.5, 4.3-4.4; only figure is the PRM flowchart
findings.problem: No roadmap or tree is ever shown; the Voronoi bias, zigzag roadmap paths, wandering RRT branches and RRT* straightening are described only in words and tables
findings.whyItMatters: Standards 6.8: the main concept is how samples cover free space; the reader must imagine it, so the 37% excess and the zigzag stay abstract
findings.action: Add one figure generated from the article's own runs: plane map with a PRM and its query path and an RRT and its first path for a stated seed, with the optimal path; optionally the RRT* tree
findings.acceptance: Figure present near 2.3 or 3.5, readable at 1280 and 360 px in light and dark, seed and parameters match the text, caption says what to notice

findings.location: Section 4.2, r_n and gamma_PRM display; mobile-light-32
findings.problem: At 360 px the line ends at gamma_PRM >, hiding the threshold
findings.whyItMatters: It is the section's result and Exercise 1 uses it; the worked example restates it only for d = 2
findings.action: Put r_n and the threshold on separate lines
findings.acceptance: Both formulas fully visible at 360 px

findings.location: Section 4.3, 'The original proof of RRT*'s'; desktop-light-19, mobile-light-34
findings.problem: Apostrophe after the asterisk typeset as a left single quotation mark (RRT*‘s)
findings.action: Write U+2019 in the source or rephrase
findings.acceptance: Correct apostrophe or no possessive on new captures
